_note: SYNTH's judgement, read by tools/synthesize.py: which automate and amplify tasks make one thing to build, the build pattern and target autonomy, the North Star input, value stream step, lean waste, the build brief and golden demo, and the inputs for financial and quality lines. Placeholders in braces ({hours_removed}, {fte}, {labour_eur}, {value_eur}, {pct_removed}, {first_extra_eur}) are filled by the script. Every assumption is for a fictional company and carries a grade: replace it with a measured figure (E4) before using a number outside this exploration.

annual_revenue_eur.label: annual revenue EUR
annual_revenue_eur.note: fictional; about EUR 125k per employee, a plausible range for Dutch logistics and warehousing (model knowledge)

dso_days_saved_billing.label: DSO days saved
dso_days_saved_billing.note: invoices out on working day 1 instead of later; to measure

duplicate_payment_rate.label: duplicate or wrong payment rate
duplicate_payment_rate.note: model knowledge: a fraction of a percent of spend; check against AFAS history

flex_spend_eur.label: agency spend EUR
flex_spend_eur.note: 225 flex workers on average (company profile: 150 to 300) x 1,600 h x EUR 30/h agency rate (assumed)

agency_invoice_error_rate.label: agency invoice error rate
agency_invoice_error_rate.note: hours or rates billed that do not match the hours worked; to measure on three months of invoices

hires_per_year.label: hires a year
hires_per_year.note: 20% turnover on 1,200 employees; warehouse turnover is often higher (model knowledge)

cost_per_vacancy_day.label: cost per open day EUR
cost_per_vacancy_day.note: overtime or agency premium while a warehouse role is open

cost_per_early_leaver.label: cost per early leaver EUR
cost_per_early_leaver.note: recruiting, induction and lost productivity; assumption

payroll_error_rate.label: payslips corrected afterwards
payroll_error_rate.note: measure the share of payslips corrected after payday

cost_per_payroll_error.label: cost per correction EUR
cost_per_payroll_error.note: about an hour of payroll and HR time plus the employee's time

long_absence_cases.label: absence cases over 6 weeks a year

wage_sanction_cost.label: cost of a wage sanction EUR
wage_sanction_cost.note: a UWV loonsanctie extends wage payment by up to 52 weeks; about a year of loaded warehouse pay (model knowledge)

certificate_renewals.label: certificate renewals a year
certificate_renewals.note: forklift, VCA and food safety for about 750 operational staff; assumption

cost_per_lapse.label: cost per lapse EUR
cost_per_lapse.note: an operator off the truck for a shift plus a rush booking; assumption

audit_fee_reduction.label: fee reduction
audit_fee_reduction.note: if the auditor relies on the controls file; assumption

opportunities.name: Answer desk for HR and finance questions
opportunities.summary: Employees, team leaders and budget holders ask in Teams. Answers come from the CAO, the handbook, the finance procedures and the asker's own AFAS record, with the source shown. Anything personal or unclear goes to a named person.
opportunities.pattern_why: An answer needs several sources (two CAOs, the handbook, an AFAS record) and a rule for when to hand over. A person approves anything that changes someone's pay, contract or leave.
lean_waste: motion: searching CAO PDFs, files and old mails
waiting: questions sit in an inbox
overprocessing: the same answer written again
opportunities.route_to_cash: HR administrator and HRBP hours move to onboarding and site visits; no extra HR hire when the flex pool grows in the season.

build_brief.what: A Teams assistant that answers HR and finance procedure questions from approved sources and hands over to a named person when it should.
components: approved source library on SharePoint (both CAOs, handbook, finance procedures), an owner per document
retrieval that cites article and page
read-only AFAS lookup of the asker's own contract, leave balance and scale
handover rules (pay, contract, health, conflict, anything not covered) into the HR case list
weekly review of answers marked wrong or unclear
data: CAO Beroepsgoederenvervoer and the warehouse CAO
AFAS employee, contract and leave data (own record only)
finance procedures: expenses, purchasing, budget rules
build_brief.first_slice: Leave and holiday questions for one site, in Dutch and English, from the warehouse CAO and AFAS leave balances.
build_brief.done_when: 70% of leave questions answered without HR over four weeks, with no answer the HR administrator marks as wrong.

golden_demo.trigger: At 02:10 a night-shift order picker in Venlo asks in Teams, in English, whether Easter Monday pays 150% or 200% and how many leave hours they have left.
golden_demo.messy_case: They are on the transport CAO, not the warehouse CAO, because they moved from driver's mate last year. The handbook PDF still shows last year's rate.
golden_demo.artefact: An answer that cites the transport CAO article and the AFAS contract record, gives the leave balance from AFAS, and notes that the handbook page is out of date.
golden_demo.approval_gate: Because handbook and CAO disagree, the answer goes out on the CAO rate and a flag lands with the HR administrator, who approves the handbook correction.
golden_demo.closes_loop: The handbook page is corrected on SharePoint, the old version leaves the source library, and the question is logged under public holiday pay.
golden_demo.business_number: {hours_removed} hours a year back for HR and finance ({fte} FTE, {labour_eur}).

opportunities.name: Case briefing and file notes for HR business partners
opportunities.summary: Before a conversation the HRBP gets a one-page briefing: contract, history, CAO articles, similar past cases and options. Afterwards a draft file note and follow-up mail. The conversation stays human.
opportunities.pattern_why: The value is trust and judgement in the room. AI prepares and writes up; the HRBP decides and signs.
lean_waste: overprocessing: file notes written from memory
motion: facts collected from AFAS, mail and PDFs
opportunities.route_to_cash: Each HRBP covers more team leaders and spends the time on the floor at the three sites instead of behind a screen.

build_brief.what: A case copilot in Microsoft 365 that builds a one-page briefing from AFAS and the case list, and drafts the file note from the HRBP's dictated points.
components: case list on SharePoint with a case type
briefing template: facts, CAO basis, precedent, options with risks
dictation to draft file note and follow-up mail
library of approved wording for warnings and agreements
data: AFAS contract, scale, absence and earlier file notes
build_brief.first_slice: Salary and classification complaints at one site.
build_brief.done_when: Preparation time per case halves over 20 tracked cases, and every file note is approved by the HRBP before it reaches AFAS.

golden_demo.trigger: A team leader in Tilburg logs that a reach-truck driver refuses Saturday shifts and says their scale is wrong.
golden_demo.messy_case: The driver moved from the transport CAO to the warehouse CAO last year, the function description on SharePoint dates from 2019, and Rotterdam handled a similar case differently.
golden_demo.artefact: A one-page briefing with contract history, both CAO articles, the Rotterdam precedent and three options with their risks; after the meeting, a draft file note and follow-up mail.
golden_demo.approval_gate: The HRBP edits and approves the file note before it is filed in AFAS. Nothing reaches the employee without them.
golden_demo.closes_loop: Agreed actions become dated reminders, the outcome joins the precedent library, and the outdated function description is flagged to C&B.
golden_demo.business_number: {hours_removed} HRBP hours a year back ({labour_eur}), spent on the floor.

opportunities.name: Employee listening and early leaver signals
opportunities.summary: Pulses at day 7, 30 and 60, exit notes and complaints are read and themed every week per site and shift, so HR and team leaders act before people leave in their first 90 days.
opportunities.pattern_why: Open comments are unstructured. A model turns them into themes per site and shift inside a fixed weekly report that a person checks.
lean_waste: inventory: survey comments nobody reads
waiting: problems found at the exit interview
opportunities.route_to_cash: Fewer early leavers means fewer replacement hires and less agency premium while roles are open.

build_brief.what: A weekly listening report: short pulses at day 7, 30 and 60, exit reasons and complaints, themed by site, shift and team, with suggested actions.
components: pulse questions in Forms or Teams in Dutch, English and Polish
theme coding against a fixed code book the HRBPs own
nothing shown for groups under five people
Power BI page joined to AFAS start and leave dates
action log per site
data: AFAS start and leave dates per team
build_brief.first_slice: The day-30 pulse for new hires in Venlo with a weekly theme report to the site HRBP.
build_brief.done_when: Every new hire gets the day-30 pulse, themes are reviewed weekly, and 90-day retention is reported per team.

golden_demo.trigger: Monday 07:00: the week's day-30 pulses and two exit notes for Venlo are in.
golden_demo.messy_case: Comments mix Dutch, English and Polish, one names a team leader, and three mention the same night bus that leaves before the shift ends.
golden_demo.artefact: A one-page Venlo report: top themes with counts and quotes (names removed), 90-day retention by team, and two suggested actions.
golden_demo.approval_gate: The HRBP checks the themes and removes anything that could identify a person before the report goes to the site manager. Groups under five stay hidden.
golden_demo.closes_loop: The bus action is logged with an owner, and the next pulse asks whether it changed.
golden_demo.business_number: {hours_removed} hours a year of report work back, plus {first_extra_eur} a year if early leaving drops as assumed.

opportunities.name: Screening and selection assistant with a fairness check
opportunities.summary: Applications in Recruitee are read against the vacancy's written must-haves, with the reasons shown. The recruiter decides. Criteria and tests are checked for adverse impact before they go live.
opportunities.pattern_why: CVs and letters are unstructured; the output is a checkable match per criterion. Recruitment is high risk under the EU AI Act, so a person decides every rejection.
lean_waste: waiting: applicants sit unread for days
overprocessing: every CV read in full for a forklift role
opportunities.route_to_cash: Roles fill sooner, so less overtime and agency premium on open warehouse roles; recruiters take on hiring that agencies do today.

financial.name: Shorter vacancies
financial.note: shared with candidate messages and sourcing; counted here only

build_brief.what: A Recruitee integration that checks each application against the vacancy's must-haves, quotes its evidence, and never rejects on its own.
components: must-haves and nice-to-haves per vacancy, approved by the hiring manager
a match per criterion with a quote from the CV
review screen in Recruitee: invite, reject, ask
monthly adverse-impact report per vacancy
logging and a human oversight file for the EU AI Act
data: past hiring decisions, for testing only
build_brief.first_slice: Order picker and reach-truck vacancies at one site, the recruiter deciding every application.
build_brief.done_when: Median time from application to first contact under two working days, recruiters agree with 90% of the must-have checks, and no group's pass rate falls below four-fifths of the highest group's.

golden_demo.trigger: A new application lands in Recruitee for a reach-truck driver vacancy in Tilburg.
golden_demo.messy_case: The CV is in Polish with a Dutch summary, the forklift certificate is a phone photo, and the work history has a two-year gap.
golden_demo.artefact: A match card in Recruitee: certificate found and valid (read from the photo), Dutch level unknown, gap noted but not scored, next step a phone screen.
golden_demo.approval_gate: The recruiter decides; the tool cannot reject. A gap is never a criterion, and the monthly fairness report goes to the HR director.
golden_demo.closes_loop: The decision and its reason are logged in Recruitee for the AI Act file, and the candidate gets a status message the same day.
golden_demo.business_number: {hours_removed} recruiter and HR admin hours a year ({labour_eur}), plus {first_extra_eur} a year from shorter vacancies as assumed.

opportunities.name: Candidate messages that go out on time
opportunities.summary: Every stage change in Recruitee sends the right message in the candidate's language, and questions about pay, shifts and travel get answers from the vacancy and the CAO.
opportunities.pattern_why: Simplest first: status messages are rules on stage changes in a fixed workflow, and one model call answers questions from the vacancy and the CAO. Nothing plans across steps, so no agent. A recruiter approves rejections after interview and every offer.
lean_waste: waiting: candidates chase for news
motion: the same mail copied again
opportunities.route_to_cash: Fewer candidates drop out while waiting, so fewer vacancies reopen and fewer roles go to agencies.

build_brief.what: Stage-triggered candidate messages and a question answerer in Recruitee, in Dutch, English and Polish.
components: templates per stage and language
Recruitee webhook on stage change
answers on pay, shifts, travel and contract from the vacancy and the CAO
recruiter approval for rejections after interview and for offers
alarm when a candidate has waited three working days
build_brief.first_slice: Status messages for warehouse vacancies at all three sites.
build_brief.done_when: No candidate waits more than three working days for news, measured in Recruitee.

golden_demo.trigger: On Friday afternoon a hiring manager moves eight candidates to 'rejected after interview' in Recruitee.
golden_demo.messy_case: Two of them asked a question in their last mail (a night allowance, a bus to Venlo), and one is a flex worker who fits another open role.
golden_demo.artefact: Eight drafts: five standard, two that answer the question first, and one flagged 'internal candidate: suggest the open Rotterdam role'.
golden_demo.approval_gate: The recruiter approves the batch in one screen. Rejections after an interview never go out unapproved.
golden_demo.closes_loop: Messages are logged in Recruitee, the flex worker moves to the Rotterdam vacancy, and the waiting clock resets.
golden_demo.business_number: {hours_removed} hours a year back ({labour_eur}), and no candidate waits more than three days.

opportunities.name: Vacancy text, sourcing and internal match
opportunities.summary: From a staffing request to a published vacancy, a channel plan, search strings and the employees and flex workers who already fit, in one pass.
opportunities.pattern_why: The recruiter and HRBP decide where to look and whom to approach; AI drafts the vacancy, the search strings and the internal shortlist.
lean_waste: skills unused: good flex workers and employees overlooked
motion: vacancies rewritten from scratch
opportunities.route_to_cash: Internal and flex-to-permanent hires replace agency fees and shorten the time to productive.

build_brief.what: A recruiter copilot that turns a staffing request into a vacancy text, channel plan and search strings, and lists employees and flex workers who match.
components: staffing request form in Teams
vacancy drafter with the CAO scale and a salary range
internal match on AFAS functions and Studytube certificates, and on flex worker history
channel plan per role family and site
data: Recruitee past vacancies and sources of hire
build_brief.first_slice: Internal and flex match for reach-truck and team leader vacancies.
build_brief.done_when: Every vacancy shows an internal shortlist before it goes outside, and the share of internal and flex-to-permanent hires is tracked.

golden_demo.trigger: The Rotterdam site manager asks for three reach-truck drivers for the peak season, starting in five weeks.
golden_demo.messy_case: Two agency flex workers already drive reach trucks there, one with an expired certificate, and the scale in the old vacancy text is wrong.
golden_demo.artefact: A vacancy text with the right scale and salary range, a channel plan, and an internal list: two flex workers (one needs recertification, booked in Studytube) and one warehouse employee who asked for a move.
golden_demo.approval_gate: The recruiter and site manager choose whom to approach. Nothing is published or sent without them.
golden_demo.closes_loop: The vacancy is published from Recruitee, the internal candidates are contacted, and the source of each hire is logged.
golden_demo.business_number: {hours_removed} hours a year back ({labour_eur}) and fewer roles going to agencies.

opportunities.name: Joiner, mover and leaver flow from Recruitee to AFAS and payroll
opportunities.summary: A signed offer or a change request becomes the AFAS employee, contract, payroll data and day-one tasks, with every field checked. HR approves before payroll uses it.
opportunities.pattern_why: Several systems and exceptions (CAO, flex-to-permanent, part-time), but the end state is checkable; HR approves each mutation before payroll uses it.
lean_waste: transport: handoffs between recruiter, HR administrator and payroll
defects: re-keyed data, wrong scale or tax credit
opportunities.route_to_cash: HR administrator and payroll hours absorb the seasonal flex-to-permanent wave without temporary admin staff.

build_brief.what: An agent that turns a Recruitee hire or a manager's change request into checked AFAS mutations (employee, contract, payroll, leave) and day-one tasks.
components: Recruitee 'hired' webhook and a change request form
AFAS UpdateConnector calls with field checks (BSN, IBAN, scale, hours, CAO)
document check: ID, signed contract, payroll tax form
approval screen for the HR administrator
day-one checklist: badge, Studytube courses, safety induction
build_brief.first_slice: New hires in warehouse functions on the warehouse CAO.
build_brief.done_when: 90% of new hires reach AFAS without re-keying, no first payslip needs a correction, and onboarding completed in week one is reported.

golden_demo.trigger: A candidate signs the offer in Recruitee for an order picker role in Venlo, starting in nine days.
golden_demo.messy_case: They work there now as an agency flex worker (their history matters for the chain of fixed-term contracts), they want 32 hours, and the IBAN on the form has a typo.
golden_demo.artefact: A ready AFAS employee and contract mutation at the right scale for 32 hours with the flex history noted, a failed IBAN check with a mail asking the new hire to correct it, and the Studytube induction booked.
golden_demo.approval_gate: The HR administrator approves the mutation in one screen; payroll only sees it after approval.
golden_demo.closes_loop: The contract goes out for e-signature, the start sits in the day-one checklist, and payroll gets a confirmed record.
golden_demo.business_number: {hours_removed} hours a year back for HR administration and payroll ({labour_eur}).

opportunities.name: Personnel file intake and employer statements
opportunities.summary: Documents that arrive by mail (certificates, signed forms, requests for an employer statement) are read, filed in the AFAS dossier and answered.
opportunities.pattern_why: Incoming documents are unstructured; the output is a filed document with a type and date, or a filled employer statement, which a person checks.
lean_waste: inventory: documents waiting in the HR inbox
motion: files searched to answer a request
opportunities.route_to_cash: HR administrator time moves to onboarding and to answering people in person.

build_brief.what: A mailbox reader that classifies HR documents, files them in the right AFAS dossier and drafts replies such as an employer statement for a mortgage (werkgeversverklaring).
components: HR mailbox listener
document classifier with a fixed list of types
AFAS dossier upload with type, date and expiry
employer statement filled from AFAS data
review queue for uncertain items
build_brief.first_slice: Employer statements and certificate scans.
build_brief.done_when: The HR inbox is empty at the end of each day and employer statements go out within one working day.

golden_demo.trigger: Monday morning: 46 mails in the HR inbox.
golden_demo.messy_case: A bank asks for an employer statement for someone on a fixed-term contract; a forklift certificate scan is upside down; one mail contains medical details that must not be filed.
golden_demo.artefact: Forty-three documents filed in AFAS with type and expiry, a drafted employer statement with the right salary and contract fields, and a warning on the medical mail.
golden_demo.approval_gate: The HR administrator signs the employer statement and decides what happens to the medical mail; the tool never files health information.
golden_demo.closes_loop: The statement is sent, the certificate expiry feeds the training planner, and the inbox is at zero.
golden_demo.business_number: {hours_removed} hours a year back for the HR administrators ({labour_eur}).

opportunities.name: Job descriptions, grading and pay ranges
opportunities.summary: One function house: descriptions, CAO grading and pay ranges in one place, drafted with AI and checked by C&B, ready for the EU pay transparency rules.
opportunities.pattern_why: Grading is a judgement with works council and pay consequences. AI drafts descriptions, compares them with the CAO grid and spots inconsistencies; C&B decides.
lean_waste: defects: descriptions out of date, scales that differ by site
overprocessing: descriptions written from scratch
opportunities.route_to_cash: Fewer grading complaints, and the pay gap work is done in house instead of by a consultant.
quality_text: EU Pay Transparency Directive (2023/970): salary ranges in vacancies and gender pay gap reporting, with a joint pay assessment when an unexplained gap of 5% or more appears (model knowledge, E1; check the Dutch implementation date)

build_brief.what: A function house on SharePoint with AI-drafted descriptions graded against the CAO function grid, linked to AFAS functions, and a pay gap check in Power BI.
components: description template and drafts from O*NET tasks and interviews
grading assistant that compares with the CAO reference functions and explains its score
link to AFAS function codes and scales
pay gap and outlier report per function and gender
data: CAO function grids and reference functions
build_brief.first_slice: The 20 warehouse and transport functions with the most people.
build_brief.done_when: Every AFAS function has a current description and grade, and the pay gap report runs from AFAS without manual work.

golden_demo.trigger: A team leader asks to regrade 'reach-truck driver' because the job now includes stock counts on the handheld.
golden_demo.messy_case: Three versions of the description exist, two sites pay different scales for the same work, and one site's scale was agreed with the works council in 2021.
golden_demo.artefact: One updated description, a grading proposal against the CAO reference function with its reasoning, and the people affected with their current scales and the effect on the pay range.
golden_demo.approval_gate: C&B and the HR director decide; a regrading with pay effects goes to the works council.
golden_demo.closes_loop: AFAS function codes are updated, old versions are retired, and the pay gap report is rerun.
golden_demo.business_number: {hours_removed} C&B hours a year back ({labour_eur}) and a pay gap report ready when the law asks for it.

opportunities.name: Workforce and personnel cost planner
opportunities.summary: One model of heads, hours and cost per site and function, with CAO raises, flex mix and the season as scenarios, shared by HR and Finance.
opportunities.pattern_why: The arithmetic is deterministic, the choices are not. The HR director and controller pick scenarios; AI builds the model, runs variants and explains them.
lean_waste: overprocessing: the spreadsheet rebuilt every budget round
defects: HR and Finance with different head counts
opportunities.route_to_cash: Better flex-versus-permanent decisions lower agency spend; one head count saves reconciliation time in HR and FP&A.

build_brief.what: A driver-based workforce model (FTE, hours, flex, CAO raises, overtime) per site, refreshed from AFAS and the agency CSVs, with a copilot that runs and explains scenarios.
components: driver model on the AFAS extract
agency hours and rates from the weekly CSVs
CAO raise and allowance tables
scenario runner with a written explanation
monthly plan versus actual
data: AFAS heads, contracts, hours and salaries
volume forecast per site from operations
build_brief.first_slice: The personnel cost forecast for one site, with flex mix as the main lever.
build_brief.done_when: HR and Finance use one head count, and the personnel cost forecast is within 2% of actuals over three months.

golden_demo.trigger: The CAO parties agree a raise from 1 July, and Venlo's biggest customer adds a second shift from September.
golden_demo.messy_case: Venlo runs a large flex share in peak; agency rates follow the CAO raise through the hirer's pay rule a month later; two people on long-term sick leave are still paid.
golden_demo.artefact: Three scenarios (more flex, more permanent, mixed) with cost per month, FTE per site and the effect on the budget, plus a one-page explanation.
golden_demo.approval_gate: The HR director and controller choose the scenario that goes into the forecast.
golden_demo.closes_loop: The chosen scenario feeds FP&A's forecast and the hiring plan; actuals are compared every month.
golden_demo.business_number: {hours_removed} hours a year back ({labour_eur}) and one personnel cost number for HR and Finance.

opportunities.name: Labour market, CAO and regulation radar
opportunities.summary: A weekly brief on what changed that matters for Noordhaven: the labour market per region, competitor pay and vacancies, CAO and law changes, customer news.
opportunities.pattern_why: Simplest first: a fixed source list on a schedule is a workflow, not an agent; model calls summarise each source with a link per claim, and the analyst checks claims and links before the brief goes out.
opportunities.value_stream_step: know the labour market before the vacancy
lean_waste: motion: reading many sources by hand
overproduction: reports nobody asked for
opportunities.route_to_cash: Analyst and specialist time moves from collecting to advising; pay and hiring decisions in tight regions are made earlier.

build_brief.what: A scheduled workflow over a fixed source list that writes a sourced weekly brief and keeps a dated change log.
components: source list: CBS, UWV labour market data, CAO texts, the government gazette, competitor career pages, customer news
fetch and summarise with a link per claim
change log by topic
analyst review step
Teams post to the HR and Finance leads
data: Noordhaven's open vacancies and pay ranges for comparison
build_brief.first_slice: Labour market and competitor vacancy pay for Venlo and Tilburg.
build_brief.done_when: A brief goes out every Monday, every claim has a link the analyst opened, and the HR director uses it in the monthly review.

golden_demo.trigger: Monday 06:00, the weekly run.
golden_demo.messy_case: A competitor in Venlo raised its posted order picker pay, a bill on flex contracts was amended in parliament, and one source is an undated vendor blog.
golden_demo.artefact: A one-page brief: three changes that matter, each with a link and what it means for Noordhaven, and the vendor blog listed as unconfirmed.
golden_demo.approval_gate: The people analyst checks every claim and link before the brief is posted.
golden_demo.closes_loop: The pay comparison goes into the Venlo vacancy review, and the law change joins the HR director's watch list.
golden_demo.business_number: {hours_removed} hours a year back ({labour_eur}) for analysis instead of collection.

opportunities.name: Payroll check before the run: hours, allowances, leave and mutations
opportunities.summary: Before every run, hours, leave, allowances and mutations are checked against the CAO rules and the last three periods; only the exceptions reach the payroll specialist.
opportunities.pattern_why: CAO allowance and leave rules can be written down, the inputs are structured and the result is checkable: build it with AI coding, run it without a model.
lean_waste: defects: corrections after payday
overprocessing: every line checked by hand
opportunities.route_to_cash: Payroll hours move to agency invoice checks and pay data work; fewer corrections after payday.

build_brief.what: A rule engine that compares the period's hours, allowances, leave and mutations with the CAO rules and the last three periods, and lists the exceptions with a reason.
components: CAO allowance rules as tested code (shift, overtime, public holiday, night)
import of hours and leave from AFAS
variance check per employee against the last three periods
exception list with rule, reason and suggested fix
sign-off record per run
data: AFAS hours, leave and mutations for the period
build_brief.first_slice: Shift and public holiday allowances under the warehouse CAO.
build_brief.done_when: Every run has a signed exception list, and corrections after payday halve over three months.

golden_demo.trigger: Three days before the monthly run, the hours for 1,200 employees are final in AFAS.
golden_demo.messy_case: Easter Monday fell in the period, a team in Tilburg swapped shifts without updating the roster, and one employee went from 40 to 32 hours mid-month.
golden_demo.artefact: An exception list of 21 lines out of 1,200: the wrong holiday rate on 9, a missing night allowance on 11 after the shift swap, and a pro-rata error on the hours change, each with the rule and the fix.
golden_demo.approval_gate: The payroll specialist approves each fix in AFAS and signs off the run.
golden_demo.closes_loop: Fixes are booked before the run, the sign-off is stored with it, and the roster owner gets a note about the swap.
golden_demo.business_number: {hours_removed} payroll hours a year back ({labour_eur}) and {first_extra_eur} a year of corrections avoided as assumed.

opportunities.name: Payroll close: reconciliation, payslips and filings
opportunities.summary: After the run, the payroll journal, the salary batch, the bank statement and the payroll tax return are reconciled automatically and the reports go out; the payroll specialist reviews the differences.
opportunities.pattern_why: Reconciliation and filing are rules on structured data; differences go to a person.
lean_waste: overprocessing: totals ticked by hand
waiting: the ledger waits for payroll
opportunities.route_to_cash: Payroll closes on payday, so the month close does not wait; the hours freed absorb head count growth.

build_brief.what: Automatic reconciliation of the payroll journal, the SEPA salary batch, the CAMT.053 statement and the payroll tax return (loonaangifte), with a difference report.
components: payroll journal to ledger check
SEPA batch to CAMT.053 match
payroll tax return totals to payroll totals
pension and statistics reports from AFAS
difference report with sign-off
build_brief.first_slice: Bank batch to statement, and journal to ledger.
build_brief.done_when: Payroll is reconciled on the day of payment with no manual ticking.

golden_demo.trigger: Payday: the SEPA salary batch is executed and the CAMT.053 statement arrives.
golden_demo.messy_case: Two payments bounced on closed accounts, and a retroactive raise for 40 people was paid in a separate run.
golden_demo.artefact: A reconciliation showing the two bounced payments with names and amounts, the separate run matched to its journal, and the payroll tax totals agreeing.
golden_demo.approval_gate: The payroll specialist approves the re-payments and signs the reconciliation.
golden_demo.closes_loop: The bounced payments are reissued, the bank details are corrected in AFAS, and payroll is closed in the ledger.
golden_demo.business_number: {hours_removed} hours a year back ({labour_eur}) and payroll closed on payday.

opportunities.name: Absence case agent and benefits administration
opportunities.summary: Every sickness case follows the Wet verbetering poortwachter calendar: steps, letters and deadlines are prepared, the arbo service and insurer are informed, and HR approves each step.
opportunities.pattern_why: Many steps with fixed deadlines across AFAS, the arbo service and the insurer, plus exceptions; health and legal risk are high, so a person approves every letter and report.
opportunities.value_stream: absence to return (verzuim, Wet verbetering poortwachter)
lean_waste: waiting: deadlines missed or met at the last moment
transport: handoffs between team leader, HR, arbo service and insurer
opportunities.route_to_cash: Wage sanctions avoided, faster return to work, and lower premiums on the absence insurance.

build_brief.what: An agent that runs the poortwachter calendar per case: the problem analysis, the plan of approach, the week 42 notice to UWV, the first-year evaluation, and the reminders to the right person.
components: case calendar from the AFAS absence record
drafts of letters and forms per step
reminders to team leader, employee and arbo service
insurer and pension fund notifications
dossier check before week 91 (reintegration report)
build_brief.first_slice: Calendar and reminders for every case longer than six weeks.
build_brief.done_when: No poortwachter deadline is missed over six months, and every dossier passes the week 91 check.

golden_demo.trigger: Week 6 of a sickness case: the arbo service's problem analysis arrives by mail.
golden_demo.messy_case: The employee works part-time at two sites, the team leader changed last month, and the employee recovered in week 4 and fell ill again within four weeks, so the periods add up.
golden_demo.artefact: A drafted plan of approach naming both sites and the current team leader, the correct start date, and a calendar to week 104.
golden_demo.approval_gate: The HR administrator and the employee sign the plan. No letter goes out without HR approval, and no medical details are stored.
golden_demo.closes_loop: Deadlines sit in the calendar, the insurer is notified, and the week 42 UWV notice is scheduled.
golden_demo.business_number: {hours_removed} hours a year back ({labour_eur}) and {first_extra_eur} a year of wage sanctions avoided as assumed.

opportunities.name: Course and work instruction builder
opportunities.summary: Work instructions, safety inductions and courses drafted from SOPs and short recordings, in Dutch, English and Polish, reviewed by L&D and published in Studytube.
opportunities.pattern_why: Source material is unstructured (SOPs, photos, recordings); the output is a structured course with a quiz that L&D checks.
lean_waste: overprocessing: courses built from scratch
waiting: new hires start before the material is ready
opportunities.route_to_cash: L&D builds more courses with the same people, and experienced pickers spend less time on ad-hoc instruction.

build_brief.what: A pipeline from an SOP or a phone recording to a Studytube micro-course with a quiz, in three languages, with an L&D review step.
components: intake: SOP document, photos or a short video
draft course and quiz in plain language
English and Polish versions, each checked by a reader of that language
Studytube upload
review checklist for safety content
build_brief.first_slice: Week-one inductions for order pickers at one site.
build_brief.done_when: Every new function has a week-one course in three languages, and onboarding completed in week one is above 90%.

golden_demo.trigger: Tilburg introduces a new voice-picking procedure next month.
golden_demo.messy_case: The SOP is a 14-page Word file with old screenshots, the safety part sits in a separate PDF, and half the pickers read Polish best.
golden_demo.artefact: A 12-minute Studytube course in Dutch, English and Polish with a five-question quiz and the safety steps first.
golden_demo.approval_gate: L&D and the site safety officer approve the course before it is published; a team leader who reads Polish checks that version.
golden_demo.closes_loop: The course is assigned to every picker in Tilburg, completions are tracked, and wrong quiz answers point to unclear steps.
golden_demo.business_number: {hours_removed} L&D hours a year back ({labour_eur}).

opportunities.name: Practice simulator for team leaders
opportunities.summary: Team leaders practise the hard conversations (absence call, appraisal, warning, interview) in an AI role-play, then with L&D or the HRBP.
opportunities.pattern_why: Practice and feedback with the person in charge; the value is the skill, not a document.
lean_waste: skills unused: team leaders promoted without practice
opportunities.route_to_cash: Better conversations lower early leaving and absence; L&D reaches every team leader instead of a few a year.

build_brief.what: A role-play tool with Noordhaven scenarios that gives feedback against a conversation checklist, used before a live session.
components: scenario library written with the HRBPs
voice or text role-play in Teams
feedback against the checklist
booking of a live session with L&D or the HRBP
progress recorded in Studytube
data: CAO and policy rules per scenario
build_brief.first_slice: The absence call for new team leaders.
build_brief.done_when: Every new team leader has practised three scenarios in their first two months.

golden_demo.trigger: A newly promoted team leader in Rotterdam has to call an employee on day 3 of a sickness report.
golden_demo.messy_case: The employee is defensive and mentions trouble with a colleague, and the team leader is tempted to ask about the diagnosis, which they may not do.
golden_demo.artefact: A ten-minute role-play with feedback: asked about the diagnosis (not allowed under the AVG), did not ask what work is still possible, agreed the next contact well.
golden_demo.approval_gate: No gate on practice; L&D owns and reviews the scenario library and the feedback rules.
golden_demo.closes_loop: The team leader books a 30-minute live session, the scenario is marked done in Studytube, and common mistakes feed the course.
golden_demo.business_number: {hours_removed} L&D and HRBP hours a year back ({labour_eur}) and every team leader practised.

opportunities.name: Training planning, certificates and effect
opportunities.summary: Certificate expiry triggers enrolment, sessions are planned around shifts, and training cost and effect are reported without spreadsheets.
opportunities.pattern_why: Expiry dates, rosters and room capacity are structured data with clear rules.
opportunities.value_stream_step: certified before the first shift, and kept certified
lean_waste: waiting: operators off the truck while a certificate is renewed
motion: sessions planned by mail
opportunities.route_to_cash: No operator idle because of an expired certificate; L&D time moves to course quality.

build_brief.what: A planner that watches certificate expiry in Studytube, enrols people, books sessions around their shifts and reports cost and completion per site.
components: expiry watch on Studytube certificates
session planner using AFAS rosters and room capacity
Outlook invitations
cost per course and site
effect report: completion, quiz results, incidents
build_brief.first_slice: Forklift and VCA renewals at all sites.
build_brief.done_when: No certificate expires unplanned for three months.

golden_demo.trigger: Studytube shows 31 forklift certificates expiring in the next 60 days across the three sites.
golden_demo.messy_case: Eight of the operators work nights, the external trainer has only two dates in Venlo, and one operator is on long-term sick leave.
golden_demo.artefact: A plan of four sessions matched to shifts and the trainer's dates, drafted invitations, the sick operator held back, and the cost per site.
golden_demo.approval_gate: The L&D specialist confirms the plan before the invitations go out.
golden_demo.closes_loop: Attendance and the new certificate dates are recorded in Studytube, and the cost report updates.
golden_demo.business_number: {hours_removed} L&D hours a year back ({labour_eur}) and {first_extra_eur} a year of lapses avoided as assumed.

opportunities.name: Ask-the-data assistant on the HR and finance Power BI model
opportunities.summary: Managers and HR ask questions in plain language and get numbers from the governed Power BI model with the definition shown; the analyst handles what is new.
opportunities.pattern_why: A question in plain language becomes a query on the governed model; the answer shows the measure and filters so it can be checked; new measures go to the analyst.
lean_waste: waiting: report requests in a queue
overproduction: standard reports nobody opens
opportunities.route_to_cash: The people analyst stops producing standard reports and builds the analysis that changes decisions.

build_brief.what: A Teams assistant on the Power BI semantic model that answers with the measure, filters and definition shown, and declines when a group is too small.
components: curated semantic model with described measures
question to query with the measure shown
minimum group size and role-based access
log of unanswered questions
monthly review of the top questions
data: Power BI dataset on the nightly AFAS extract
build_brief.first_slice: Absence rate, head count, hires and leavers per site and month.
build_brief.done_when: Half of today's ad-hoc report requests are answered by the assistant, checked by the analyst on a sample.

golden_demo.trigger: The Venlo site manager asks in Teams: 'What was absence on night shift last quarter against day shift, and how many of the long cases are new hires?'
golden_demo.messy_case: Shift is not a field in AFAS but a roster code, 'long case' needs a definition, and one night team has only four people.
golden_demo.artefact: An answer with both absence rates, the definition used (longer than six weeks), the roster mapping shown, and the small team left out.
golden_demo.approval_gate: None for answers from approved measures; a new measure or mapping goes to the people analyst first.
golden_demo.closes_loop: The shift mapping becomes a governed measure, and the question joins the list of answered questions.
golden_demo.business_number: {hours_removed} analyst and HR admin hours a year back ({labour_eur}).

opportunities.name: BI build pipeline: from request to tested Power BI change
opportunities.summary: Report and dashboard changes are specified, built, tested and documented with AI coding tools on the Power BI model, and released after review.
opportunities.pattern_why: The output is code (DAX, SQL, Power Query) that can be tested; AI writes it faster and it runs without a model.
lean_waste: defects: broken measures found by users
waiting: changes queue for weeks
opportunities.route_to_cash: One analyst maintains HR and finance reporting without an outside BI contractor.

build_brief.what: The Power BI model in source control, AI coding for measures and queries, automatic tests on known numbers, and generated documentation.
components: Power BI project files in Git
a test set of known numbers per measure
AI coding assistant for DAX and Power Query
generated data dictionary
release checklist
build_brief.first_slice: The HR dataset in source control with tests for the ten most used measures.
build_brief.done_when: Every change ships with passing tests and an updated dictionary, and a request reaches release within a week.

golden_demo.trigger: Finance asks for agency hours per site next to employee hours on the absence dashboard.
golden_demo.messy_case: Agency hours arrive as weekly CSVs from three agencies with different column names, and one agency counts breaks as hours.
golden_demo.artefact: A tested Power Query that maps the three formats, a new measure, the dashboard page, and a dictionary entry.
golden_demo.approval_gate: The people analyst reviews the change and the tests before release; the controller confirms the agency hours match the invoices.
golden_demo.closes_loop: The change is released, the tests run on every refresh, and the request is closed.
golden_demo.business_number: {hours_removed} analyst hours a year back ({labour_eur}).

opportunities.name: Invoice to payment: capture, match, code, approve, pay
opportunities.summary: Supplier and agency invoices are read, matched to the purchase order or the agency hours, coded and routed for approval in AFAS; the payment batch is proposed to the controller.
opportunities.pattern_why: PDF invoices are unstructured; the output, a coded booking matched to an order, is checkable inside a fixed AFAS workflow; exceptions and payments go to a person.
lean_waste: overprocessing: every line keyed and checked
motion: approvers chased by mail
defects: duplicate and wrong payments
opportunities.route_to_cash: Bookkeeper hours absorb volume growth without a hire; duplicate payments and agency overbilling are stopped.

financial.name: Duplicate and wrong supplier payments stopped

build_brief.what: An invoice pipeline: read from the mailbox, match to the order or the agency hours, code, approve in AFAS, and propose a weekly SEPA payment batch.
components: e-invoices (UBL) first, PDF reading second
match to AFAS purchase orders, and to agency hours from the weekly CSVs
coding suggestion from supplier history
approval routing by budget holder in AFAS
duplicate and bank-change checks
SEPA batch proposal for the controller
data: agency hours CSVs and rate cards
build_brief.first_slice: Invoices from the three staffing agencies, matched to hours.
build_brief.done_when: 60% of invoices booked without touch, every agency invoice matched to hours, and no duplicate paid in a quarter.

golden_demo.trigger: A staffing agency's weekly invoice for Tilburg arrives as a PDF in the AP mailbox on Monday.
golden_demo.messy_case: It bills 1,312 hours while the agency's own CSV says 1,288, four workers are billed at the night rate for day shifts, and the agency changed its bank account last week.
golden_demo.artefact: A coded booking in AFAS with the 24-hour gap and the four rate errors listed per worker, and the payment on hold because of the bank change.
golden_demo.approval_gate: The bookkeeper sends the dispute; the controller confirms the bank change by phone before the next payment batch.
golden_demo.closes_loop: A credit note is requested and matched when it arrives, the bank change is confirmed and logged, and the invoice is paid in the next SEPA run.
golden_demo.business_number: {hours_removed} hours a year back ({labour_eur}) plus {first_extra_eur} a year of wrong payments stopped as assumed.

opportunities.name: Bank statement matching: cash application and reconciliations
opportunities.summary: Every CAMT.053 statement is matched to open items and ledger accounts automatically; only real differences reach a person.
opportunities.pattern_why: Bank lines, open items and ledger balances are structured; matching rules can be written and tested.
lean_waste: overprocessing: lines ticked by hand
inventory: unmatched items piling up
opportunities.route_to_cash: Bookkeeper hours freed; cash is known every morning, so collections and the cash forecast start from today's position.

build_brief.what: A matching engine on CAMT.053 and AFAS open items with rules for references, amounts, partial and combined payments, and a short exception list.
components: daily CAMT.053 import
rule-based matching (invoice number, amount, IBAN, combinations)
a model call for free-text remittance only when the rules fail
suspense account report
balance sheet reconciliation checklist
build_brief.first_slice: Customer receipts on the main Rabobank account.
build_brief.done_when: 95% of bank lines match automatically and every balance sheet account is reconciled by working day 3.

golden_demo.trigger: The morning CAMT.053 statement with 412 lines arrives from Rabobank.
golden_demo.messy_case: A large customer pays seven invoices in one amount, minus a disputed pallet charge, with a remittance text that quotes their PO numbers instead of the invoice numbers.
golden_demo.artefact: 411 lines matched; the combined payment split over seven invoices, the short payment left open as a dispute and linked to the collections case.
golden_demo.approval_gate: The bookkeeper decides between write-off and dispute; the tool never writes anything off.
golden_demo.closes_loop: Open items are cleared in AFAS, the dispute goes to the collections officer, and the bank account is reconciled for the day.
golden_demo.business_number: {hours_removed} hours a year back ({labour_eur}).

opportunities.name: Credit and collections agent
opportunities.summary: Overdue accounts are found every day, reminders go out in the right tone, disputes and promises are tracked, new customers get a credit check, and the officer handles the hard calls.
opportunities.pattern_why: Several steps, tools and exceptions (disputes, promises, escalation); the officer approves escalations and anything beyond a standard reminder.
lean_waste: waiting: reminders sent late
motion: history looked up before every call
opportunities.route_to_cash: Cash comes in sooner, write-offs fall, and the officer's time goes to the large accounts.

financial.name: Cash in sooner (financing cost saved)
financial.note: the one-off cash freed is revenue / 365 x days saved

build_brief.what: An agent that runs the dunning calendar per customer from AFAS, drafts reminders and replies, logs promises and disputes, and prepares the officer's call list.
components: daily overdue list from AFAS with a risk score
reminder drafts by stage and customer type
reply reader for promises, disputes and questions
dispute routing to operations with the delivery proof
credit check for new customers (KvK and payment history)
handover to a collection agency only after approval
data: AFAS receivables, payment history and customer contacts
build_brief.first_slice: Reminder stages 1 and 2 for every customer below a set balance.
build_brief.done_when: DSO falls by the assumed days over two quarters, with no complaint from a key account.

golden_demo.trigger: Day 15 overdue: a mid-sized retailer has EUR 84,300 open across nine invoices.
golden_demo.messy_case: They answered the last reminder that two invoices are disputed for damaged pallets, promised the rest 'end of month', and their accounts payable contact has changed.
golden_demo.artefact: A reply confirming the promise for seven invoices with a date, a damage dispute opened with the delivery proofs, and the new contact in AFAS.
golden_demo.approval_gate: The collections officer approves the reply and the dispute; a delivery stop or a handover to a collection agency needs the finance director.
golden_demo.closes_loop: The promise date is tracked and the payment matched when it arrives; the dispute is closed with operations.
golden_demo.business_number: {hours_removed} hours a year back ({labour_eur}) and {first_extra_eur} a year from cash coming in sooner as assumed.

opportunities.name: Customer invoicing and cost calculation
opportunities.summary: Invoices for storage, handling and transport are built from contract rates and activity data and checked before they go out.
opportunities.pattern_why: Contract rates and activity volumes are structured and the invoice is checkable: build it once, run it every month.
lean_waste: defects: invoice errors that customers dispute
waiting: invoices go out days after month end
opportunities.route_to_cash: Invoices go out on working day 1 with fewer disputes, so cash comes in sooner.

build_brief.what: A billing engine that applies contract rates to monthly activity (pallet places, order lines, transport) and creates checked sales invoices in AFAS.
components: contract rate tables per customer
activity import from the warehouse and transport systems (not in today's system list; to confirm)
rate engine with indexation (fuel, CAO)
variance check against last month
AFAS invoice creation
build_brief.first_slice: Storage and handling invoices for the ten largest customers.
build_brief.done_when: All invoices out on working day 1, and disputes over invoice errors halved.

golden_demo.trigger: Month end: the activity exports for every customer are ready.
golden_demo.messy_case: One contract's fuel surcharge changed mid-month, and another customer's pallet count jumps 60% because of a mis-scanned location.
golden_demo.artefact: Draft invoices with the split fuel surcharge applied, and the pallet jump flagged next to last month's figure.
golden_demo.approval_gate: The bookkeeper reviews the flagged invoices before they are sent; the rest go out on day one.
golden_demo.closes_loop: Invoices are posted in AFAS and sent; the mis-scan goes back to the warehouse.
golden_demo.business_number: {hours_removed} hours a year back ({labour_eur}) and {first_extra_eur} a year from earlier cash as assumed.

opportunities.name: Month-end close assistant: journals, accruals and checklist
opportunities.summary: Recurring journals, accruals and depreciation are prepared from data, the close checklist runs itself, and the accountant reviews and posts.
opportunities.pattern_why: Many steps and sources with new exceptions every month; each journal is approved before it is posted.
lean_waste: waiting: close tasks waiting on each other
overprocessing: the same journals rebuilt every month
opportunities.route_to_cash: The close gets shorter, and accountant hours go to analysis and controls.

build_brief.what: A close agent that runs the checklist, prepares accruals (agency hours not yet invoiced, energy, bonuses), recurring and depreciation journals, and trial balance checks.
components: close checklist with owners and dependencies
accrual drafts from agency hours, open purchase orders and contracts
depreciation from the asset register
trial balance variance review with explanations
posting after approval
data: AFAS ledger, open purchase orders, asset register
build_brief.first_slice: The agency hours accrual and the recurring journals.
build_brief.done_when: Days to close down by two over three months, with no audit adjustment on the automated journals.

golden_demo.trigger: Working day 1 of the close.
golden_demo.messy_case: Last week's agency hours are in the CSVs but not invoiced, one agency's CSV is missing, and a new forklift lease started mid-month.
golden_demo.artefact: An accrual journal for the uninvoiced agency hours (the missing agency estimated from its last four weeks), a lease journal, and a trial balance with three variances explained.
golden_demo.approval_gate: The accountant reviews and approves each journal before posting; the controller signs off the close.
golden_demo.closes_loop: Journals are posted in AFAS, the checklist shows done, and the accruals reverse next month when the invoices arrive.
golden_demo.business_number: {hours_removed} hours a year back ({labour_eur}) and fewer days to close.

opportunities.name: Management reporting pack with commentary
opportunities.summary: The monthly pack (profit and loss, balance sheet, cash, KPIs per site) builds itself after the close with a first draft of the commentary; the controller edits and signs.
opportunities.pattern_why: The numbers come from a fixed model; one model call drafts the commentary from the variances, and the controller checks it.
lean_waste: overprocessing: numbers pasted into slides
waiting: the board waits for the pack
opportunities.route_to_cash: Controller and finance director hours go to decisions with the sites instead of formatting.

build_brief.what: A monthly pack generated from the closed ledger in Power BI and PowerPoint, with draft commentary on the main variances per site.
components: fixed pack template
variance finder (budget, last year, forecast) per site
commentary drafts that quote the numbers
board and bank covenant reports from the same data
sign-off step
build_brief.first_slice: The site profit and loss pages with commentary.
build_brief.done_when: The pack is ready one day after the close, and the controller edits rather than writes.

golden_demo.trigger: The close is signed off on working day 5.
golden_demo.messy_case: Venlo's margin fell three points through higher agency rates, a customer credit note and a one-off repair, and the bank's covenant report needs the same EBITDA.
golden_demo.artefact: A pack whose Venlo page explains the three causes with amounts, and a covenant calculation from the same numbers.
golden_demo.approval_gate: The controller edits the commentary and the finance director approves the pack before it goes to the board and the bank.
golden_demo.closes_loop: The pack is filed, board questions are logged, and next month's pack carries the follow-ups.
golden_demo.business_number: {hours_removed} hours a year back ({labour_eur}).

opportunities.name: Budget intake, checks and variance commentary
opportunities.summary: Budget files from the sites are checked for completeness and consistency and summarised with a recommendation; monthly variances are explained per cost centre.
opportunities.pattern_why: Budget files and comments are semi-structured; the checks are rules, the summary and variance text come from a model, and FP&A decides.
lean_waste: defects: incomplete or inconsistent budget files
waiting: budget holders wait for feedback
opportunities.route_to_cash: FP&A hours move from checking to analysis; spending outside the budget is spotted in the month, not the quarter.

build_brief.what: A budget intake that checks each site's file against rules and last year and writes a summary with a recommendation, plus monthly variance comments per cost centre for the budget holder to confirm.
components: budget template with validation rules
consistency checks (head count against personnel cost, volume against agency hours)
summary and recommendation draft
monthly variance comments per cost centre
confirmation by the budget holder in Teams
build_brief.first_slice: Monthly variance comments for the three sites.
build_brief.done_when: Every cost centre has a confirmed variance comment by working day 6, and budget files pass the checks before review.

golden_demo.trigger: The Tilburg site sends its budget file for next year.
golden_demo.messy_case: Personnel cost assumes 85 FTE while the head count tab says 92, agency hours stay flat while volume grows 12%, and one cost centre is missing.
golden_demo.artefact: A check report with the three issues, a summary recommending the file goes back, and a suggested fix for the agency hours.
golden_demo.approval_gate: The FP&A analyst decides whether to return the file and approves the summary for the finance director.
golden_demo.closes_loop: The corrected file comes back, the checks pass, and the budget is loaded into AFAS.
golden_demo.business_number: {hours_removed} FP&A hours a year back ({labour_eur}).

opportunities.name: Rolling forecast and scenarios for profit and cash
opportunities.summary: A driver-based rolling forecast of profit and a 13-week cash forecast, with scenarios (volume, CAO, fuel, a customer won or lost) explained so the business can follow them.
opportunities.pattern_why: The model is deterministic, the judgement is not: AI builds and runs scenarios and writes the explanation; the controller and finance director choose.
lean_waste: overprocessing: the forecast spreadsheet rebuilt
waiting: a scenario takes days
opportunities.route_to_cash: Better cash timing (less overdraft, surplus put to work) and decisions on customers and pricing made with numbers in hours, not weeks.

build_brief.what: A driver model (volume per site, rates, agency mix, CAO, fuel) feeding a 12-month profit forecast and a 13-week cash forecast, with a copilot that runs and explains scenarios.
components: driver model linked to AFAS actuals
13-week cash forecast from open items, payroll and the payment calendar
scenario runner
plain-language explanation per scenario
forecast accuracy tracking
build_brief.first_slice: The 13-week cash forecast.
build_brief.done_when: Forecast accuracy is tracked monthly, and the 13-week cash forecast is within 5% at week four.

golden_demo.trigger: Sales hears that a large customer may move 30% of its volume out of Venlo in the second quarter.
golden_demo.messy_case: The customer pays late, the Venlo lease runs for years, and agency staff can go quickly but permanent staff have CAO notice periods.
golden_demo.artefact: Two scenarios (lose the volume, or keep it at a price cut) with profit, cash and FTE effects per month, and a one-page explanation.
golden_demo.approval_gate: The finance director and controller decide what goes to the board.
golden_demo.closes_loop: The chosen scenario updates the forecast, HR's workforce plan is adjusted, and the outcome is later compared with actuals.
golden_demo.business_number: {hours_removed} hours a year back ({labour_eur}) and a forecast the business trusts.

opportunities.name: VAT and tax filings from AFAS
opportunities.summary: The VAT return, the EU sales listing and the corporate tax workpapers are prepared from AFAS with checks, ready for the controller and the outside adviser.
opportunities.pattern_why: Tax codes and return boxes are rules on structured ledger data; the controller approves every filing.
lean_waste: overprocessing: boxes mapped by hand
defects: wrong VAT codes found late
opportunities.route_to_cash: Accountant and controller hours freed; fewer corrections and a smaller bill from the outside tax adviser.

build_brief.what: The VAT return and EU sales listing generated from AFAS with code checks (reverse charge, intra-EU, import), plus workpapers for the corporate tax return.
components: VAT code and box mapping with tests
checks on unusual codes and missing VAT numbers
EU sales listing (ICP)
corporate tax workpaper pack for the adviser
filing sign-off
build_brief.first_slice: The checks on the VAT return.
build_brief.done_when: The VAT return is prepared in an hour with every exception explained.

golden_demo.trigger: The month is closed and the VAT return is due.
golden_demo.messy_case: A German carrier's invoice was booked with Dutch VAT instead of reverse charge, and a Belgian customer's VAT number is invalid.
golden_demo.artefact: A draft VAT return listing both exceptions with the correcting entries proposed.
golden_demo.approval_gate: The controller approves the corrections and the return before filing.
golden_demo.closes_loop: The corrections are booked, the return is filed, and the customer's VAT number is updated.
golden_demo.business_number: {hours_removed} hours a year back ({labour_eur}).

opportunities.name: Continuous controls monitoring and audit file
opportunities.summary: Key controls (segregation of duties, bank detail changes, duplicate suppliers, journal approvals, payroll changes) are tested on all transactions every week, and the audit file builds itself.
opportunities.pattern_why: Control tests are rules on AFAS data; a model only drafts the finding text; the controller owns the result.
lean_waste: defects: errors found by the auditor months later
overprocessing: samples tested by hand
opportunities.route_to_cash: A lower audit fee and fewer adjustments; problems are found the week they happen.

build_brief.what: A weekly controls run on AFAS data with findings, owners and evidence, and an audit file per control for the external auditor.
components: control library with tests (segregation of duties, bank changes, duplicates, journals without approval, payroll changes)

finding text drafts

build_brief.first_slice: Bank detail changes and duplicate suppliers.
build_brief.done_when: Every key control is tested weekly, and the auditor relies on the file for two controls.

golden_demo.trigger: The weekly run on Sunday night.
golden_demo.messy_case: A supplier's bank account was changed by the same user who approved its invoice, and two supplier records share an IBAN under slightly different names.
golden_demo.artefact: Two findings with evidence and draft text, assigned to the controller.
golden_demo.approval_gate: The controller decides on each finding and confirms the bank change with the supplier by phone.
golden_demo.closes_loop: The duplicate supplier is merged, the user's rights are split, and the evidence is filed for the auditor.
golden_demo.business_number: {hours_removed} hours a year back ({labour_eur}) and {first_extra_eur} a year off the audit fee as assumed.
